subject: Renewal discussion — capacity uplift + term amendment
messages:
From: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@aurora-ai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Narang <priya@aurora-ai.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning + usage spike — Aurora AI

Hi Aditya,

Quick note as we head into our contract renewal window: over the last 3 months our prod usage has increased ~3x as we rolled out the new assistant to two more product lines. Procurement wants a clear renewal path and visibility into pricing if we commit to higher capacity.

High level asks from our side:
- 12 month price hold if we increase committed units by 40%
- One-time credit to offset Q2 overage while the new commit ramps up
- Clear timeline for contract signature (procurement needs it by end of month)

Attaching the current usage export for context. Can we set up a quick call this week to walk numbers?

Thanks,
Jordan
Director of Platform, Aurora AI

Attachment: Aurora_Current_Usage_Report.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@aurora-ai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + usage spike — Aurora AI

Thanks Jordan — good to see the ramp. I pulled your run rates and a couple of options that should meet procurement timelines:

Option A (preference for larger customers):
- +40% committed units, 12-month price hold, 5% one-time onboarding credit applied as invoice credit
- Commitment starts on renewal effective date; overage billed at standard committed overage rate

Option B (shorter commitment runway):
- +25% committed units, 9-month price hold, larger one-time credit to smooth Q2 costs

I attached a draft term amendment (v1) with placeholders for the commit numbers — legal will need to redline. Proposed next steps: 
1) 30 min sync tomorrow to confirm target option
2) I loop in contracts and your procurement to finalize language

If procurement insists on a 12-month price hold and a legal-mandated SLA credit, we'll need approval from Marissa for that level of concession.

- Aditya
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Narang <priya@aurora-ai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@aurora-ai.com>, Legal <contracts@aurora-ai.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + usage spike — Aurora AI

Aditya/Laura — thanks for the quick response. Procurement is firm on two constraints:
1) We need a 12-month price hold tied to the increased commit (they consider anything shorter too risky during Q3 product launches).
2) The one-time credit should be explicit on the amendment and applied to the first post-renewal invoice.

We can sign quickly if you can commit to the 12-month hold and provide a simple credit line. We prefer plain-language amendment we can circulate internally.

Priya
Head of Procurement, Aurora AI

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priya Narang <priya@aurora-ai.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + usage spike — Aurora AI

Priya — appreciate the clarity. To balance risk we can propose a middle path that preserves unit economics for both parties:

- 12-month price hold but with a stepped commit schedule: 40% uplift guaranteed across 12 months, with a 20% upfront increase effective at renewal and the remainder ramped in month 4.
- One-time credit = 4% of projected Q2 invoice (applied to first post-renewal invoice).
- If Aurora exceeds 150% of committed consumption in any month, overage reverts to standard overage rates (this protects unit economics).

I've updated the term amendment and attached a redline (Proposed_Term_Amendment_v2.pdf). If this is acceptable, Marissa will need to approve the final concession level (discount/credit).

Thanks,
Laura
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Proposed_Term_Amendment_v2.pdf (pdf, 68KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Legal <contracts@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@aurora-ai.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning + usage spike — Aurora AI

Forwarding Laura's proposal to contracts. Summary for legal:
- Approve 12-month price hold tied to a 40% committed uplift (stepped schedule as drafted)
- Approve one-time credit equivalent to 4% of Q2 projected invoice (documented in amendment)
- Hard stop: no additional SLA credits beyond the standard SLA; overage protection clause as in the redline is acceptable

If legal signs off quickly, we should route the DocuSign for Aurora procurement and aim to close by 2027-04-15. DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/appointments/ABCDEF-2027

-Marissa
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
